question:
If $p \rightarrow (p \wedge \sim q)$ is false. Truth value of $p \& q$ will be
यदि $p \rightarrow (p \wedge \sim q)$ असत्य है, तब $p \& q$ का सत्यता मान होगा
explanation:
Truth table analysis:

| $p$ | $q$ | $\sim q$ | $p \wedge \sim q$ | $p \rightarrow (p \wedge \sim q)$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | F | F | F |
| T | F | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | F | T |
| F | F | T | F | T |

Thus, $p$ and $q$ are both True (TT) when $p \rightarrow (p \wedge \sim q)$ is false.
subject: Mathematics

question: The negation of '$\sqrt{5}$ is an integer or $5$ is an irrational number' is

options.text: $\sqrt{5}$ is an integer and $5$ is not an irrational Number
$\sqrt{5}$ is not an integer and $5$ is an irrational Number
$\sqrt{5}$ is not an integer or $5$ is not an irrational Number
$\sqrt{5}$ is not an integer and $5$ is not an irrational Number

explanation:
Let $p$: $\sqrt{5}$ is an integer, $q$: $5$ is an irrational number.
Given statement is $p \vee q$.
Its negation is $\sim(p \vee q) \equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q$.
Thus, '$\sqrt{5}$ is not an integer and $5$ is not an irrational number'.
subject: Mathematics

question: The contrapositive of the statement "If I reach the station in time, then I will catch the train" is:

options.text: If I will catch the train, then I reach the station in time
If I do not reach the station in time, then I will catch the train
If I do not reach the station in time, then I will not catch the train
If I will not catch the train, then I do not reach the station in time

explanation:
Let $p$: I reach the station in time, $q$: I will catch the train.
Given statement is $p \rightarrow q$.
Contrapositive is $\sim q \rightarrow \sim p$, which means 'If I will not catch the train, then I do not reach the station in time'.

question: Contrapositive of the statement \"If two numbers are not equal, then their squares are not equal\". :

If the squares of two numbers are equal, then the numbers are equal.

question: If $p$ : weather is good, $q$ : ground is not wet. Write the negation of $p \wedge q$.

options.text: weather is not good or ground is wet
weather is good or ground is wet
weather is not good and ground is wet
weather is good and ground is not wet

explanation:
Using De Morgan's Law, $\sim (p \wedge q) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q$.
Since $p$ is 'weather is good', $\sim p$ is 'weather is not good'.
Since $q$ is 'ground is not wet', $\sim q$ is 'ground is wet'.
Thus, $\sim (p \wedge q)$ means 'weather is not good or ground is wet'.
subject: Mathematics
